title: Towards Efficient SRAM-PIM Architecture Design by Exploiting Unstructured Bit-Level Sparsity
problem: Traditional SRAM-PIM architectures with rigid crossbars cannot effectively exploit unstructured bit-level sparsity in neural networks. Eliminating redundant calculations on randomly distributed zero-bits requires flexible hardware support.
motivation: Bit-level sparsity can significantly boost computational efficiency and reduce energy consumption in neural network accelerators.
method: DB-PIM combines software optimization with custom hardware to skip wasted computations on scattered zeros (bit-level sparsity) in neural network weights. It uses a dyadic block pattern—a way to organize these zeros that keeps them randomly distributed but limits how many appear per weight—making the pattern structured enough for hardware to reliably detect and skip. Specialized multiplication units (DBMUs) and efficient adders (using Canonical Signed Digit encoding) perform the calculations, while an input preprocessing unit applies similar zero-skipping to incoming data.
key_novelty: The dyadic block sparsity pattern—keeping zeros randomly distributed while constraining their count—paired with custom hardware units (DBMUs and CSD-based adders) designed specifically to exploit it.
contributions: Dyadic block sparsity pattern that maintains accuracy while improving computational regularity
Custom PIM macro with dyadic block multiplication units and CSD-based adder trees
Input pre-processing unit for block-wise input sparsity exploitation
Achieves 7.69× speedup and 83.43% energy savings over baseline PIM
limitations: Evaluation details and comparison with other sparsity exploitation methods not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: Exploiting unstructured bit-level sparsity in SRAM-PIM via algorithm-architecture co-design
